t: This is The Glass House in Fulham, a building made for one purpose: a stained-glass studio and workshop. Mary Lowndes and Alfred Drury went into partnership in 1897, and in 1906 they had it built for independent stained-glass artists to work in. The architect was C. H. B. Quennell, who was also a designer, illustrator and historian. A heritage architect says his influence can be felt in the houses and streets of London's suburbs. He also wrote books that drew children and young people into history.
